report.summary: Reviewed chunk 4 of 4 of daedalus/structcore/graph.py: contains function docstring and implementation for reachability calculation.
risks: line 361 | medium | Docstring claims fenced modules are excluded, but code uses fenced_fragment to define fenced set; fenced_fragment not defined in chunk. | Verify fenced_fragment implementation in same module or imported file.

line 375 | medium | Docstring claims multi-source BFS over forward edges from fenced set; code uses reverse logic (forward edges from fenced, but comment says 'reverse graph' earlier). | Clarify direction of edges in idx['import_edges'] and ensure consistency.
line 386 | low | Sorting frontier and nodes may impact performance; docstring mentions O(V*E) concern but sorting adds O(V log V). | Confirm performance requirements.
line 396 | low | Comment about guardrail failing toward disable is not enforced in code; behavior depends on caller. | Check how fraction=0.0 is handled by guardrail logic.

handoff.purpose: Implement reachability calculation for fenced modules.

symbols.name: fenced_fragment
symbols.note: Referenced but not defined in this chunk; used to determine if a node is fenced.

symbols.name: candidates
symbols.note: Set of nodes not in fenced set.

symbols.name: escalated
symbols.note: List of candidate nodes reachable from fenced set.

claims.text: DENOMINATOR CHOICE (deliberate): already-fenced modules are excluded.
claims.why: Code computes candidates = nodes - fenced, excluding fenced nodes from denominator.

claims.text: Computed as ONE multi-source BFS over the forward edges from the fenced set
claims.why: Code initializes frontier = sorted(fenced) and performs BFS using forward edges from fwd dictionary.

claims.text: a module reaches a fenced node in the reverse graph exactly when it is reachable from a fenced node in the forward graph
claims.why: The chunk does not define 'reverse graph' or verify equivalence; BFS uses forward edges from fenced nodes, which finds nodes reachable from fenced, not nodes that reach fenced.

claims.text: not V separate BFS runs -- the router calls this on every task and O(V*E) on a 7k-file repo is not something a fence may cost.
claims.why: Performance claim about router calls and repo size cannot be verified from this chunk alone.

claims.text: No non-fenced candidates -> 0.0, which keeps the guard ON. A guardrail that fails toward 'disable the fence' is the wrong failure.
claims.why: Code returns fraction=0.0 when candidates list is empty.

observations.what: Docstring describes multi-source BFS over forward edges from fenced set; code implements BFS using fwd dictionary.
Function fenced_fragment is referenced but not defined in this chunk; its behavior is critical to correctness.
The BFS uses sorted() on frontier and nodes; sorting may have performance implications.
